meta.title: Nadia's Otters
meta.textType: functional: a fact file in an email, with headings

paragraphs: Dear Mia, this is Nadia, and here is my fact file about otters. I wrote it on Monday, July twenty-seventh. Mia, I know that you love animals, too. I love animals and photography. This fact file has three parts, and each part has a heading. Last month, I took several photos of wild otters in a park near my home. I have just sent you my best photo. In my photo, three otters sit on a rock in the sun. A wild otter looks like a long, brown cat with short legs.

Where otters live. Otters live near rivers and ponds. Some otters live near the sea. Otters live in small groups near the water. A river is a good home for them. They make a home in a hole next to the water. Otters like quiet places with clean water. They are wild creatures, so we must stay far away.

What otters eat. Otters eat fish, especially small fish. They also eat crabs and frogs. A hungry otter eats a lot every day. The otters in my park eat fish in the morning. I watched an otter with a fish in its mouth.

What otters do. Otters swim fast, and they go under the water. An otter can stay under the water for a long time. They have soft fur, and the fur keeps them warm. Otters sound like birds when they call each other. Otters and dogs are similar, because both like to play. An otter family has about six otters. They play together, and they make me happy. In my photos, they look happy when they play.
What else do you want to know about otters? Do you have otters in Thailand? Do you like them? Do you have a favorite wild creature, Mia? Please write back soon. Best wishes, Nadia.
text.summary: Nadia writes an email to Mia with a fact file about otters. It has three headings, and Nadia asks Mia two questions about otters in Thailand.
